questions.question: How do I build a granular sampler in Pd that plays short grains from a recorded sample?
questions.notes: Describes playing many short segments in rapid succession (the Sampling section), reads the sample from an array with tabread4~ or tabplay~, schedules the grains, and windows each one. Should distinguish the documented mechanism from the starting values it suggests.

questions.question: Why does my grain cloud click, and how do I stop it?
questions.notes: Explains the discontinuity at grain edges (Enveloping samplers) and fixes it with an envelope that reaches zero at both ends: line~ per grain, or cos~ for a signal-rate window. Mentions that window shape and overlap trade off.

questions.question: How do grain duration and read rate set the pitch of a granular sampler?
questions.notes: Uses the looping-sampler transposition relation from the Sampling section rather than inventing a rule: transposition is the read rate relative to the sample's own rate, scaled by the segment length. Should not present a particular grain size as a documented default.

questions.question: How do I keep a dense grain cloud from getting too loud or clipping?
questions.notes: Points out that overlapping grains sum, so level has to be scaled deliberately; suggests checking with env~ (RMS dB) and clip~ to detect overload, and putting gain under a smoothed line~ control.

questions.question: Can I use [tabplay~] instead of [tabread4~] for the grains?
questions.notes: Explains the trade-off from the object pages: tabplay~ plays a table segment without transposition and without interpolation artifacts, so it is cheaper; tabread4~ interpolates and is what changes pitch. A good answer names which one fits the user's goal.

questions.question: How do I freeze a sound in Pd so a short moment keeps sustaining?
questions.notes: Frames freezing as granular playback with a fixed read position and overlapping windowed grains; grounds it in the Sampling / enveloping samplers sections; flags grain size and overlap numbers as suggestions.

questions.question: How can I time-stretch a recording without changing its pitch in Pd?
questions.notes: Explains the looping-sampler / granular approach: scan the read position slowly while each grain plays at the original rate, so transposition and speed are decoupled; quotes the Sampling section rather than inventing formulas.

questions.question: What window shape should I use for my grains, and how do I make one with [cos~]?
questions.notes: Says the envelope must be zero at both ends (enveloping samplers), shows scaling a phase ramp into the positive half of [cos~] as the book does, and marks the specific shape choice as a suggestion rather than a documented standard.

questions.question: How do I load a sound file into an array to use as the source for grains?
questions.notes: Uses [soundfiler] to read into an [array define] (or graph) array, loaded before DSP starts; suggests a $0- prefixed name if the patch is instantiated more than once; cites the Arrays chapter.

questions.question: How do I add random scatter to the position and pitch of each grain?
questions.notes: Uses a control-rate scheduler ([metro] + [random]) to set each grain's start position and rate before firing its envelope, starting deterministic and adding scatter; keeps reads inside the array; ranges flagged as suggestions.

questions.question: My granular patch makes a 'scratching' or Doppler sound when I move the position control. Why?
questions.notes: Explains that changing the read position while a grain plays changes its effective rate (the book's Doppler/scratch description); offers holding the pointer per grain with [samphold~] on the phase wrap as a fix.

questions.question: My granular patch is silent. What should I check?
questions.notes: Checks the array was actually loaded (soundfiler path/return count), DSP on, the window/line~ not stuck at zero, the scheduler actually firing; suggests printing the array or the read index; no invented causes.

questions.question: How many simultaneous grain voices can I run in Pd before CPU becomes a problem, and how do I organise them?
questions.notes: Says the docs do not give a voice limit; suggests a modest voice count with [clone] or a single signal-rate scheduler, and measuring; flags numbers as suggestions.

questions.question: What is granular synthesis, in terms of how Pd's documentation describes it?
questions.notes: Paraphrases the Sampling section's definition (many small segments of a sample in rapid succession) and relates grain duration, overlap and read position to the result, citing the book.

questions.question: How do I stop my grain read index from going past the end of the array?
questions.notes: Says to clamp or wrap the index explicitly (e.g. [clip~] or wrapping the position) based on the array size, because array indices run 0 to N-1; does not rely on out-of-range behaviour.

questions.question: Should my grains be scheduled with [metro] or with [phasor~]?
questions.notes: Contrasts control-rate scheduling (metro starts each grain with a line~ envelope) with signal-rate streams (phasor~ sweeping read position and window together, as in the book's figures), with the trade-offs; no claim that one is the documented standard.
